paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, the Explorers met in the school library, as they did every week. Teacher Kim stood beside the big table and held a modern tablet. "Today we make a video for the class blog," she said. "Mia reads her fact file about sea turtles, and the tablet records her." "Then Grace and Ravi can watch it in Singapore with their class." Mia held her paper in both hands. She folded it once, and then she folded it again.

"Excuse me, Teacher Kim," said Mia. "May I go to the toilet?" "Of course," said Teacher Kim. Mia walked out of the library with the small paper square in her hand. Five minutes passed, and then ten minutes passed. Leo looked at the door and then at the clock on the wall. "She is slow today," he said. Lily put down her pen and went out to look for her friend.

Lily found Mia in the hall beside the sink. Mia washed her hands for the third time. "Mia, is everything alright?" asked Lily. "Yes," said Mia, but she did not look at Lily. "The water is nice and cold." She dried her hands slowly, one finger at a time, and she did not pick up the paper. The paper square lay on the side of the sink.

Lily sat down on the step next to the wall. "Before my first talk, I read my post to Pip," she said. "It was a useful idea, and Pip listened well." "Pip is at home," said Mia. "That's a pity." "Then read it to me," said Lily. Mia opened the paper and held it with two hands. She read in a very quiet way, and the paper moved in her hands. "Good," said Lily. "Now a little louder."

Mia read it again, and this time her words came out louder. "I am able to hear every word," said Lily. Then the two girls walked back to the library together. Teacher Kim touched the red sign on the tablet. Mia stood among her friends and read the fact file from the first line to the last. May and Leo sat very still, and nobody made a sound. At the end, her hands were still. "Is anybody ready to watch it?" asked May. "Wait," said Mia. "Can I read it one more time?"
